deletion_lane.notes: Email Whitepages for full deletion. This route avoids the phone call in its form.

false_success_traps: A broker acknowledgement is not proof that the listing is gone.
A page saying the link to the listing is not found or not valid means the request never started.
A recheck was once recorded as a removal with no screenshot, on a site that shows browser challenges. An empty recheck with no saved proof is not a removal.
Broker confirmation does not prove removal. The scheduled check still matters.
If the call is missed or the page does not change within a few minutes, the request was not completed. Start again.
Loose words like "removed" or "successfully" elsewhere on the page are not the receipt. Look for the message that the opt-out request was accepted.
Seeing the four-digit code on the page is not a confirmation. The call must be answered and the code entered.
genuine_confirmation: After you take the phone call and enter the four-digit code, the page changes to say the opt-out request has been accepted. Nothing before that point counts.
name: Whitepages

opt_out_routes.note: The broker lists a privacy request address. Use it when the phone-code tool is not practical.

opt_out_url_check.note: A plain request got a "Just a moment..." browser check (HTTP 403). The project knowledge file records that the page loaded in a browser on 2026-11-16.

quirks: A broker acknowledgement is not proof that the listing is gone.
Broker confirmation does not prove removal. The scheduled check still matters.
Search engines may show old copies of the listing for up to 30 days.
The automated suppression tool can require a phone callback.
The opt-out has five steps. It needs no account and no email address.
Use the privacy-request email lane when a phone call is not practical.
You must take a phone call to finish the standard flow.
steps: Open your listing and copy its web link before you start.
Open the Whitepages opt-out page. Paste the link and press Next.
Check that the listing is yours. Then choose Remove Me.
Pick a reason for the request and press Next.
Enter a phone number. Whitepages calls it to check the request.
Note the four-digit code on the page. Enter it when the call asks for it.
Wait for the page to say the removal is in progress. Then plan a recheck.
